title: Smooth analytic data on complex points and holomorphic cotangent sheaves
statement: For a complex scheme $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C$ [def-pc-scheme], let $X(\mathbf C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C,X)$, with the topology generated by the inverse images of complex open sets under every local regular function. A finite-dimensional complex analytic atlas on a topological space consists of open partial homeomorphisms to $\mathbf C^n$, covering the space, with analytic coordinate changes; $n$ may vary. A function on an open is holomorphic if it is analytic in all these coordinates. A holomorphic one-form is an analytic family of complex-linear continuous covectors in these coordinates, satisfying $w_c=w_d\circ D(d\circ c^{-1})$. The holomorphic function ring sheaf and holomorphic cotangent module sheaf [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have exactly these sections, their pointwise operations and their restriction maps; exterior differentiation is coordinate differentiation. Smooth analytic data over $X$ comprise a ringed space whose points and topology are the preceding $X(\mathbf C)$, such an atlas whose chart coordinates are local regular functions on affine opens, its holomorphic function sheaf and cotangent sheaf, and a morphism $\pi$ to $X$ sending a complex point to its underlying scheme point and every regular function to its evaluation. For an algebraic module sheaf $F$, define $F^{\mathrm{an}}=\mathcal O_M\otimes_{\pi^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\pi^{-1}F$ using the canonical inverse-image module structure and sheafified scalar extension [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; the local tensor $h\otimes s$ is the tensor-presheaf section followed by sheafification. A closed holomorphic embedding means a closed topological embedding analytic in coordinates with injective coordinate derivative. For a morphism $i:X\to Y$ over $\mathbf C$, the induced map of analytic point sets is composition $x\mapsto i\circ x$.

source.place: Serre, GAGA, nos. 1, 4--6, no. 5 remark p. 9, no. 9 Definition 2, pp. 16--17; analytic covectors and derivative embedding criterion expanded in lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent steps 6 and 9--10. Read online https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf.
